title: Frontend: Implement a Stack
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Implement a Stack. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(commands). Commands are {type:push,value}, pop, peek, or size. Return one output per command; push returns size, and empty pop/peek return null.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep the backing array private and expose operations with documented empty behavior.
alternativeApproaches: Add a minimum-value operation using an auxiliary minimum stack with duplicate minima handled correctly.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty pop/peek; undefined value; repeated pushes/pops.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
